To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lowest 900 microwave resonances of two superconducting constant-width billiards are described by the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble of random-matrix theory, and that the tunnel splitting distribution can be described by an analytical expression.

the lowest 900 microwave eigenvalues of two constant-width billiards coincide with those of the corresponding random matrix ensemble and that dynamical tunneling can be quantified in terms of a splitting distribution that is derived from the random-matrix ensemble.
the lowest 900 microwave resonances of two superconducting resonators with a rectangular cross section and different aspect ratios can be described with high accuracy by a random matrix model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between classical chaos and quantum dynamics in systems with unidirectional motion.
the quantum dynamics in systems with a non-trivial classical counterpart, i.e., systems with a mixed dynamics.
the quantum dynamics of a system with unidirectional classical dynamics, which is a prototype for a large class of physical systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the constant-width billiard exhibits the properties of a mixed system, with dynamical tunneling playing a crucial role.
the two constant-width billiards exhibit dynamical tunneling and are thus quantum mechanically chaotic.
the quantum constant-width billiard is a paradigmatic system for the study of dynamical tunneling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to determine the spectral properties of two constant-width billiards in a way that has never been achieved before.
dynamical tunneling can be understood as a manifestation of the quantum-mechanical uncertainty relation.
dynamical tunneling is a generic phenomenon in quantum systems with mixed classical dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dynamical tunneling can be quantified in terms of the splitting distribution of resonance pairs.
the spectral properties of quantum billiards are not determined only by the classical dynamics, but also by the geometry of the boundary.
the random-matrix theory for quantum chaos is capable of describing tunneling effects in quantum systems with a mixed classical dynamics.
